title: ECL110 MQTT state parser takes a JSON boolean as a displacement (true -> 1.0, false -> 0.0)
claim: _parse_ecl110_state accepts the payloads 'true', 'false' and '{"displace": true}' as displacements 1.0, 0.0 and 1.0, and _async_handle_ecl110_state_message stores and publishes them as the measured ECL110 displacement, where const.finite_float refuses a bool as 'a guess, not a reading'.
mechanism: json.loads('true') is the bool True; `isinstance(data, (int, float))` admits it (bool subclasses int) and `float(raw)` turns True into 1.0, so a state topic pointed at a switch/flag topic (ON/true) or a hostile publisher sets _ecl110_current_displace and the published ecl110_displace_command/ecl110_effective_displace to a value no ECL110 reported. The plausibility window (round-9 D1-s2-02) does not catch it: 0 and 1 are inside every window.

evidence.unit: boolean payloads stored as a displacement (of 3 sent)
evidence.machine: orchestrator Mac, Apple M1 (darwin arm64, 8 cores), shared box

perturbation.change: _parse_ecl110_state refuses a bool: `elif isinstance(data, (int, float)) and not isinstance(data, bool)` and `None if raw is None or isinstance(raw, bool) else float(raw)` (`--perturb ecl110_refuse_bool`, recompiled in memory)

metric_definition: Count of the payloads 'true', 'false', '{"displace": true}' after which the handler holds a non-None _ecl110_current_displace (reset to None before each message).
phenomenon_property: An external-input parser hands on only a finite real number as a measurement: a bool is never a displacement, a temperature or a power (const.finite_float's rule), at every external parser seam.

null_control.note: the numeric payloads 7 and '{"displace": "3"}' are still accepted (2 of 2) under the perturbation: the fix refuses bools only

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._parse_ecl110_state: refuse bool at both the bare-number and the dict-member arm (or route through const.finite_float); coordinator.py only.
